name: nexus
description: A local-first second brain: search, read, and curate a folder of Markdown notes that remembers your thinking across chats.
long_description:
Nexus gives Claude a durable memory that lives in your own Markdown files instead of inside a single conversation. It indexes a folder of notes — an Obsidian vault, or any directory of .md files — and exposes six tools for finding and curating them: hybrid semantic + keyword search, full-note reads with backlinks and supersession chains, and non-destructive writes.

Everything is local. The notes stay on your disk as plain Markdown, the search index is a disposable projection you can delete and rebuild at any time, and embeddings are computed on your own machine by a model that runs offline after a one-time download. Nothing you write is transmitted anywhere.

Nexus never hard-deletes. Archiving marks a note and keeps the file; replacing a note archives the old one and cross-links both, so the path your thinking took stays recoverable. Every change is a git commit in your vault.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find notes by meaning or exact term. Fuses semantic vector search with keyword search, so both conceptual questions and rare identifiers hit. Read-only.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a full note by uid: frontmatter, body, backlinks, semantically related notes, and resolved supersession pointers. Read-only.

tools.name: upsert
tools.description: Create a new note or overwrite an existing one. Guarded against clobbering edits made outside Nexus. Can supersede an older note, which archives and cross-links it rather than deleting it.

tools.name: archive
tools.description: Mark a note as archived, removing it from active views. The file is kept on disk and the change is a git commit, so it stays recoverable.

tools.name: link
tools.description: Add an authored [[wikilink]] from one note to another, under a Links heading. Idempotent.

tools.name: reindex
tools.description: Rebuild the search index from the Markdown source of truth. Run after editing notes outside Nexus. Assigns identifiers to new notes on first run.

vault_path.title: Vault folder
vault_path.description: The folder holding your Markdown notes — an Obsidian vault, any directory of .md files, or a new empty folder for Nexus to manage. These files are the source of truth and never leave your machine. Back up an existing vault first: the initial reindex adds a uid and invisible chunk anchors to every note.
